body: This seems to fix the issue but I think the `button_up` signal should be emitted after the pressed event. Usually, it's expected to have down, pressed and up. In this order. Maybe a bool could be set here and checked at the end of the method to prevent the code duplication.

Thanks. This raises an interesting point, which is that the current (4.3) behavior is inconsistent. Normal buttons do indeed emit down->pressed->up, but dropdowns and menus have different behavior depending whether they're being opened or closed. On close, they also emit down->pressed->up. However, on open, they emit down->up->pressed. (See attached video, taken in 4.3. It only shows dropdowns, but menus behave the same.)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7918597-6069-4dd4-9791-f46cb90c5dc6

So the question is: Should the current behavior be replicated exactly, or should the open behavior be changed to match the close behavior (and other buttons)?
